__comment: Import into Grafana and pick a Prometheus datasource. Panels are grouped by the sections §11
asks for: System, API, Database, Queue, Workers, SMTP, Inbound, Campaigns, Automation,
TWO PANELS EXIST ONLY TO STOP THE OTHERS LYING, AND THEY ARE FIRST ON PURPOSE:
'Telemetry readable' — 0 means every queue number on this dashboard is a default, not a
measurement. A dashboard that cannot say this reads as healthy during a database outage.
'Registry age'       — how long this serverless instance has been alive. Counters and latency
histograms are PROCESS-LOCAL and reset on every cold start; a young registry explains a low
counter, and without it a scrape after a deploy looks like a traffic collapse.
Queue panels use edurankai_mail_queue_* which are read from Postgres on every scrape and are
therefore cluster-wide and trustworthy. Everything else is per-instance. Do not mix them in one
Several panels will be EMPTY until the corresponding call sites are instrumented. That is
intentional and matches the 'declared, never observed' column on /admin/mail/performance — an
empty panel here means nothing has been measured, not that the value is zero.
title: EduRankAI Mail — overview

panels.title: Integrity — read this before anything below
Telemetry readable
panels.description: 0 means the queue reads failed and every queue number on this dashboard is a DEFAULT, not a measurement. Silence from the alerts is not evidence of health while this is 0.

panels.title: Registry age
panels.description: Seconds since this serverless instance created its metric registry. Counters and latency histograms below are process-local and reset with it: a low counter right after a deploy is a young process, not a traffic collapse.

panels.title: Healthy MTA nodes
panels.description: Nodes that are active and whose circuit breaker is not holding them out. Zero means nothing can be delivered and mail is queueing.

panels.title: Dead letters
panels.description: Jobs that exhausted their retries. They will never run again without an operator, and requeueing them in bulk brings any poison job back with the rest.

panels.title: Queue depth by status
panels.description: Read from Postgres on every scrape, so unlike the counters this is a true cluster-wide view.

panels.title: Arrival vs drain
panels.description: The comparison that says which way the backlog is going. Depth alone does not: a deep queue that is draining is fine, a shallow one that is filling is not.

panels.title: Queue age — pending vs stuck in processing
panels.description: ABSENT means empty, not zero: the series is deliberately not emitted when there is nothing waiting. A rising `processing` line is the crashed-worker signal — claimBatch() flips a row to processing and nothing flips it back, so those rows are invisible to both the pending queue and the retry sweep.

panels.title: Pending by job kind
panels.description: Which work is backed up, not just that something is. A single kind dominating usually means one dependency is down.

panels.title: API latency
panels.description: Bucket interpolation, so the resolution is the bucket width and never better. Per-instance: a deploy shows as a discontinuity.

panels.title: Database latency
panels.description: Includes time waiting for a pooled connection. On the Supabase transaction pooler this rises under pool saturation before any individual query gets slower — so a spike here with flat slow-query stats means connection pressure, not a bad query.

panels.title: Queue wait — enqueue to claim
panels.description: The honest definition of queue latency. Grows without bound whenever arrival exceeds drain, which is why it is the SLO signal rather than depth.

panels.title: Worker processing time
panels.description: Multiply by concurrency to get the drain-rate ceiling. This is the number capacity.ts turns into a worker count.

panels.title: Delivery outcomes
panels.description: Per-instance rates. A DEFERRAL is the recipient's server asking us to come back later — it is not a failure of ours and must never be treated as node failure.

panels.title: Bounce rate
panels.description: Sustained bounces above ~5% put sending reputation at risk, and reputation damage takes weeks of careful sending to undo. Usually a list-quality problem, not an infrastructure one.

panels.title: SMTP connect vs full delivery attempt
panels.description: The gap between the two is data transfer plus remote acceptance. If connect p50 tracks message COUNT rather than staying flat, connection pooling is not working and every message is paying for a fresh handshake.

panels.title: Inbound parse time
panels.description: Scales with message SIZE, not count — the tail here is large attachments, and it is CPU spent on the request path.

panels.title: Campaign recipient generation
panels.description: The one operation whose cost is a function of AUDIENCE size rather than send rate. Read next to the recipient-count distribution.

panels.title: Workflow execution
panels.description: Long runs hold a worker slot. A wait node that blocks rather than re-queueing shows up here as a multi-second p99 and as reduced queue drain.

panels.title: Events recorded vs dropped
panels.description: Dropped events mean analytics are undercounting. Mail delivery is unaffected by design — the buffer sheds rather than blocking a send — and this panel is what stops that trade-off being silent.
